| f-001 | defect | MAJOR | The documented per-conversation serialization does not exist, and the accounting backstop is an identity rather than a check. `runner::drain` may claim and spawn multiple `SERIAL_KINDS` jobs until `worker_concurrency` is full; the default is four. Different queue keys can address the same conversation (seat versus native route, or different folders). Both polls can read one ledger high-water mark before either commits. The claimed backstop cannot detect the resulting conflict because `append_turns` defines `already_stored` as `turns.len() - accepted.len()`, making `accepted + already_stored == prepared.turns.len()` true by construction. A concrete loss path is a partial and full concurrent poll of a group-derived Claude/metrics turn: the partial body wins a turn-number conflict, the full body is labelled already stored without content comparison, and its cursor/ledger can advance past the continuation. This breaks ac-0003 and the service page's explicit serial/accounting claims. Smallest safe fix: serialize from ledger snapshot through poll commit for one conversation (or globally for ingest as the conservative first cut), and classify a conflict as already stored only after verifying the existing turn has the same canonical content/blob hash; add a concurrent partial/full-poll regression through the composed path. | /Users/jordanknight/substrate/flowspace/fs3-convo-ingest/crates/daemon/src/runner.rs:179-227; /Users/jordanknight/substrate/flowspace/fs3-convo-ingest/crates/daemon/src/convo_ingest.rs:490-543; /Users/jordanknight/substrate/flowspace/fs3-convo-ingest/crates/store/src/conversations.rs:236-275 | — | — | — | — | [ac-0003](../../plan.dd.md#acceptance-criteria) | Fresh source trace: runner loop spawns every claimed serial-kind job while tasks.len() &lt; workers; append_turns computes already_stored solely as input length minus returned inserts; the orchestrator sums those two complementary values. Existing cursor/store suites passed but contain no concurrent composed-pipeline case. |
| f-002 | defect | MAJOR | ac-0004 promises child conversations linked to their parent, but the relationship stops at an in-memory `SessionFile` and an `IngestReport` that the asynchronous worker discards. `run` maps `ingest` to unit, the submit response exposes only address/dedupe/accepted, `Conversation` has no parent field, and the conversations schema stores no parent relation. After the job settles, neither list/get nor the database can navigate from a child conversation to its parent. | f-003 | defect | MAJOR | The independent cardinality artifact and the metrics reader disagree for the covered Copilot session, while the advertised cardinality test omits that session. The generator and committed expectation require four ordinals and state that `tool.execution_*` events become items rather than records. The reader deliberately emits `tool.execution_start` as a fifth RawRecord, and its dedicated test asserts five. The only `assert_emitted_ordinals_match` loop in the metrics suite covers MAIN and SUBAGENT Claude-mirror sessions, not COPILOT, so both contradictory tests pass. This makes the impl-guide's '4 for copilot' and ac-0007 receipt's 'each also passes the cardinality claim' untrue, and leaves exactly the shared-blind-spot the cardinality amendment was meant to remove. Reviewer ruling recommendation: the reader should move to four. Fixture row 936647 is an `assistant.message` whose `toolRequests` already carries the same `toolCallId` and call payload repeated by row 936648 `tool.execution_start`; emitting both makes one call both an item and a separate turn, unlike the normalized message-turn contract used by Claude and OMP. Register the assistant record as the open call, drop the mirrored start as a record, attach completion to that assistant record, and assert cardinality equality over every fixture session including COPILOT and the zero-turn sessions. Poll-straddled completion remains a separate contract edge: the current batch-local map already drops or splits it depending on where the boundary lands, so it should be ruled explicitly rather than used to preserve the full-batch duplication. | /Users/jordanknight/substrate/flowspace/fs3-convo-ingest/docs/plans/005-convo-ingest/assets/inputs/tools/oracle_expectations.py:595-625; /Users/jordanknight/substrate/flowspace/fs3-convo-ingest/crates/testkit/fixtures/conversations/metrics_db/expectations.json:78-89; /Users/jordanknight/substrate/flowspace/fs3-convo-ingest/crates/providers/src/conversation_sources/metrics_db.rs:754-840; /Users/jordanknight/substrate/flowspace/fs3-convo-ingest/crates/providers/tests/conversation_source_metrics_db.rs:191-213,373-407 | — | — | — | — | [ac-0007](../../plan.dd.md#acceptance-criteria) | Fresh `cargo test -p fs3-providers --test conversation_source_metrics_db` passed all 16 tests: the Copilot test accepted five records while the cardinality test passed because it iterates only MAIN and SUBAGENT. `oracle_expectations.py --check` also passed, confirming the contradictory four-record expectation is the committed generated artifact rather than drift.
